item.title: 26 Introduction
item.description:
[[P1031]]SECTION VI

CHAPTER XXVI

[[Tūntrik|Tāntrik]] doctrines and [[Dharmasastra|Dharmaśāstra]]

In H. of Dh. vol. II. p. 739 while dealing with the worship of Durgā, who is also worshipped as [[Sakti|Śakti]] (cosmic power or energy ), it was stated that the influence of [[Sākta|Śākta]] worship has [[boon|been]] great throughout India and a promise was given that a brief treatment of [[Sāktiem|Śāktism]] would follow in a later volume. It is now time to deal with Śāktas and Tantras, which exercised some influence over the Purāṇas and directly and through the Purāṇas over Indian religious ritual and practices in the medieval ages.

item.title: 27 Nyāsas, Mudrās, etc
item.description:
[[P1120]]CHAPTER XXVII Nyāsas, Mudrās, Yantra, Cakra, [[Mandala,|Maṇḍala,]] etc.

One of the important items in the [[Tantrik|Tāntrik]] ritual and worship is [[nyūza|nyāsa]], which means ‘mentally invoking a god or gods, mantras and holy texts to come to occupy certain parts of the body in order to render the body a pure and fit receptacle for worship and meditation’. [[Soveral|Several]] works such as the Jayākhya-[[samhitā|saṁhitā]] ([[Patala|Paṭala]] XI), [[Prapancasāra|Prapañcasāra]] (VI), Kulārṇava (IV. 18 ff) refer to several kinds of [[nyāga|nyāsa]]; the [[Saradātilaka|Śāradātilaka]] (IV. 29-41, V. 5-7), [[Mahānirvāpatantra|Mahānirvāṇatantra]] (III. 41-43, V. 113-118) describe several varieties of [[ayāsa|nyāsa]]. [[Rāghavabhatta|Rāghavabhaṭṭa]] on [[Śārada tilaka|Śāradātilaka]] (IV. 29-41) cites numerous quotations on nyāsa from an extensive literature. There are several kinds of [[pyāsa|nyāsa]] such1 as [[Hamsanyāsa,|Haṁsanyāsa,]] [[Prapavanyāsa,|Praṇavanyāsa,]] [[Mātṛkanyisa,|Mātṛkānyāsa,]] Mantranyāsa, [[Karagyāsa,|Karanyāsa,]] [[Anganyāsa,|Aṅganyāsa,]] [[Pithanyāsa.|Pīṭhanyāsa.]] [[Pranavanyaga|Praṇavanyāsa]] is illustrated as ‘[[om|oṁ]] ām [[Brahmane|Brahmaṇe]] [[namah|namaḥ]]’, ‘[[om|oṁ]] ām [[Viṣnavo|Viṣṇave]] namaḥ’ and [[80|so]] on for all the names set out by [[Raghavabhatta|Rāghavabhaṭṭa]] on [[sāradātilaka|Śāradātilaka]] 25. 58. The [[Adganyasa|Aṅganyāsa]] (nyāsa on parts of the body) is illustrated as follows: [[om|oṁ]] [[bṭdayāya|hṛdayāya]] namaḥ, [[om|oṁ]] [[sirase|śirase]] [[svābi,|svāhā,]] [[sikhāyai|śikhāyai]] [[vaṣat,|vaṣaṭ,]] [[om|oṁ]] [[kavacıya|kavacāya]] [[hum,|huṁ,]] [[om|oṁ]] netratrayāya (or netradvayāya) [[vaṣat,|vaṣaṭ,]] [[om|oṁ]] astrāya [[phat’.|phaṭ’.]] Several Purāṇas contain provisions about [[nyasa.|nyāsa.]] The Garuḍapurāṇa (I. chapters 26, 31, 32) describes [[anganyāsa|aṅganyāsa]] as part of worship, japa and [[homa|homa.]] The [[Nāradiyapurāṇa|Nāradīyapurāṇa]] (II. 57. 13-14), the Bhāgavata (VI. 8, about 40 [[verses ),|verses),]] Brahma (60. [[35-40 )|35-40)]] provide for nyāsa of the mantras ‘[[om naino|om namo]] Nārāyaṇāya’, and ‘om [[Viṣnaye|Viṣṇave]] [[namaḥ’ The Kalikāpurāpa|namaḥ’. The Kālikāpurāṇa]] (chap. 77) deals with [[Mātýkānyāsa.|Mātṛkānyāsa.]] The [[Smrtimuktāphala|Smṛtimuktāphala]] ([[Ahnika|Āhnika]] pp. 329-331) quotes several passages dealing with nyāsa of the 24 letters of the [[Gāyatri|Gāyatrī]] ([[Rg.|Ṛg.]] III. [[62.10 )|62. 10)]] on several parts of the body, meditation on each of the 24 letters as having certain colours of flowers and as identical with certain gods and avatāras and nyāsa of the [[Gāyatripādas|Gāyatrīpādas]] on limbs. The Brahmapurāṇa [[P1121]](60. 35-39) [[doals|deals]] with the [[Dying|nyāsa]] of the mantra ‘[[am|om]] namo [[Nārāyanāya’|Nārāyaṇāya’]] on the fingers and [[alao|also]] on other parts of the [[body.|body,]] and speaks of Karanyāsa and [[Adganyāsa|Aṅganyāsa]] in [[28. 26.|38. 26.]] [[Padus to|Padma]]2 (VI. [[79,|79.]] 17-30) describes the nyāsa of the names of [[Vishu|Viṣṇu]] on the limbs of the body from the head to the [[foot|feet]] and Padma VI. [[83.|85.]] 26 speaks of [[Anganyāds|Aṅganyāsa]] and [[Karanyasa|Karanyāsa]] with the mantra ‘om namo bhagavate [[Vasudevaya’. [The Mateyapranam|Vāsudevāya’. The Matsyapurāṇa]]3 provides for the employment in [[pyāsā|nyāsa]] of mantras with ‘om’ prefixed to them. [[Karanganyāss|Karāṅganyāsa]] and [[Anganyāsa of Gayatet|Aṅganyāsa of Gāyatrī]] are dealt with in [[Devibhagavata xI.|Devībhāgavata XI.]] 16. 76-91 and it [[ar pressly|expressly]] names nyāsa as part of sandhyā worship.4 Vide also [[Devibhagavata XI.7.26-38|Devībhāgavata XI. 7. 26-38]] for [[nyasa|nyāsa]] and [[Kalikapurapa 53.36.|Kālikāpurāṇa 53. 36.]] The [[Devibhagavata (VII,|Devībhāgavata (VII.]] 40. 6-8) mentions the [[nyāga of oartain|nyāsa of certain]] letters on such parts of the body as the [[chost,|chest,]] the space between the eyebrows, the head. The [[Brhad-yogiyajnavalkyasn|Bṛhad-yogiyājñavalkya]]5 contained [[P1122]]verses dealing with the nyāsa of the names of Viṣṇu such as Govinda, [[Mahdhara,|Mahīdhara,]] [[Ergikoda,|Hṛṣīkeśa,]] Trivikrama, [[Vipa,|Viṣṇu,]] [[Midhava OB|Mādhava on]] the fingers of the right hand and the palm and back [[rospectively,|respectively,]] which are quoted by the [[Smrtioandrika|Smṛticandrikā]] (I. p. 198) [[As|as]] from Yoga-yājñavalkya and which have been taken over in the sandhyā worship in modern times. The latter work (Sm. C. I. p. 145) also contains Aṅganyāsa of several portions of Gāyatrī, the nyāsa of the single letters of the Gāyatrī on the [[limbe|limbs]] and Aparārka (p. 140) quotes a passage for the [[employ mant|employment]] of the sixteen verses of the Puruṣasūkta (Ṛg. X. 90) for [[Ayasa|nyāsa]] on the several limbs in the worship of Viṣṇu. For the [[pyare|nyāsa]] of the letters of the alphabet from ‘a’ to ‘kṣa’, vide [[sazadetilaka|Śāradātilaka]] V. 5-8 and Rāghavabhaṭṭa on V. 4 who quotes verses setting out how each letter is to be meditated upon. The Mahānirvāṇa (V. [[176-178 )|176-178)]] also specifies the limbs on which there is to be [[ayaga|nyāsa]] of the letters of the alphabet from the forehead downwards.
